prs.title: fix(jsdoc): preserve param tags after unmatched description delimiters
prs.author: vshalpnjabi
prs.body:
## Summary

`jsdoc/require-param` reported a documented parameter as missing when the JSDoc description contained an unmatched `{` or backtick. The tokenizer stayed inside that delimiter and swallowed the following `@param`.

Reset curly-brace depth and inline (1–2) backtick spans on line terminators, matching parentheses and square brackets. Fenced code (3+ backticks) still spans lines. Balanced braces, balanced code spans, extra `}`, and `{@link}` are unchanged. A truly missing `@param` still reports.

## Test plan

- [x] Issue fixtures: unmatched `{`, unmatched backtick — fail on main, pass after
- [x] Balanced `{ a }`, `` `{ a }` ``, extra `}` stay clean
- [x] Control: documented `p` plus undocumented `q` still reports `q`
- [x] `just test -p oxc_linter`
- [x] `just lint -p oxc_linter` / `just lint -p oxc_jsdoc`
- [x] oxlint CLI repro with the issue config

## AI assistance

Drafted with AI assistance. The human opening this PR is responsible for reviewing, testing, and owning the change.

Fixes #28859.

fix(linter/eslint/no-unreachable-loop): ignore enclosing finalizers for continues
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
A `continue` inside a loop nested in `try` or `catch` stays within that protected region. Ignore the enclosing finalizer when checking whether the jump can reach another iteration, while retaining checks for finalizers inside the loop.

Adds regressions for each loop form, labeled continues, and enclosing finalizers that complete normally or return.

Fixes #28948

Regression coverage includes literal widening, static/protected members, explicit annotations, private members, and inference failures.

prs.body:
Evaluate cooked template segments and constant substitutions when emitting enum declarations. For example, `${Prefix}:click` now preserves the prefix, and `line1\nline2` emits a newline rather than a literal backslash escape. Unevaluable substitutions follow the existing runtime-initializer handling, including TS2474 for const enums.

prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Keep unused `new ArrayBuffer(...)` calls unless the length is statically valid and no options are supplied, including before normalization adds pure annotations. Preserve URI calls on potentially malformed inputs while retaining constant folding for valid inputs.

Fixes #28974.

prs.title: fix(transformer/typescript): merge exported enums across namespace blocks
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Reuse an exported enum’s existing namespace object when lowering each declaration, preserving earlier members and object identity across namespace blocks.

Adds runtime coverage for nested namespaces, private enum isolation, and enum optimization options.

Fixes #28944.

prs.title: fix(isolated-declarations): preserve object accessor mutability
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Fixes #28985

Getter-only object properties now emit `readonly`, while properties with setters remain writable even under `as const`. Accessor pairing uses JavaScript property names, so differently spelled keys such as `value` and `"value"` produce one writable property.

Regression snapshots cover accessor order, equivalent keys, and const assertions. Output mutability matches TypeScript 5.9 declaration emit.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/no-useless-undefined): narrow return type exemptions
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Match Unicorn's return-type exemptions: report `return undefined` for `void` and `undefined` return types, and check initializers and defaults regardless of the enclosing return type. Keep annotated concise arrow bodies and other annotated returns exempt.

Preserve TypeScript parameter optionality when removing defaults. Withhold fixes for unannotated TypeScript parameters, parameter properties, TypeScript destructuring defaults, and `var` initializers to preserve types and binding resets; keep reporting them. Exclude `using` declarations, whose initializers are required. Regression coverage includes defaults before required parameters and JavaScript fixes.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/prefer-negative-index): avoid panic on non-ASCII whitespace
prs.author: magurotuna
prs.body:
`unicorn/prefer-negative-index` panics if a non-ASCII whitespace character directly follows `.length`. The panic also happens without `--fix`. With Oxlint 1.91.0:

```sh
printf 'foo.slice(foo.length\xc2\xa0- 1);\n' > a.js  # U+00A0 after `length`
oxlint -A all -D unicorn/prefer-negative-index a.js
```

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates/oxc_span/src/span.rs:483:21:
end byte index 21 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u{a0}' (bytes 20..22 of string)
```

The fix sliced the source text at `member_expr_span.end + 1` to check for a space after `.length`. If the next character is multi-byte, such as U+00A0 or U+2028, this offset is inside that character.

This PR checks the text after `.length` with `starts_with(' ')` instead. The fix output does not change.

---

I used AI assistance (Claude Code) to find this bug and write this change. I reviewed the code and ran the tests.

prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
With `as-needed` and `requireReturnForObjectLiteral: true`, a TypeScript-wrapped object return could alternate between concise and block bodies on every autofix run. A parenthesized plain-object return could cycle too.

Use the same parentheses-only classification in both directions. This matches ESLint: `satisfies`, `as`, non-null assertions, and type assertions allow concise bodies, while plain objects still require explicit returns. Add regression coverage for both body forms, nested wrappers, and preserved fixes.

Also preserve right-associative `**` binding across assertions and recognize the upstream fixture’s `erasableSyntaxOnly` baseline variants. Regression coverage checks assertion chains, operand spans, and valid boundaries.

Malformed literals such as `10_;`, `0b00_;`, `0o00_;`, and `0x00_n;` currently blame the character after the underscore. Highlight the offending underscore with “Numeric separators must appear between digits” and guidance to remove it or place it between two digits.

Parsing and recovery remain unchanged. Keep `oxc_lexer`’s diagnostic bridge in sync with the parser. Existing conformance fixtures cover the regressions; 93 parser diagnostics change with no change to parser pass/fail counts or lexer differential snapshots.

prs.title: feat(linter/eslint/no-unused-vars): suggest removing unused type parameters
prs.author: YanYunCY
prs.body:
Part of #16832. Follow-up to #28730, which renamed unused type parameters to `_T`; per @camc314's review there, this removes them instead.

## What

Unused type parameters now get a dangerous suggestion (respecting `fix.variables`) that removes them:

```ts
type Foo<T> = {};                    // -> type Foo = {};
function foo<T, U>(u: U) {}          // -> function foo<U>(u: U) {}
function foo<T, U>(t: T) {}          // -> function foo<T>(t: T) {}
type Foo<T, U,> = T;                 // -> type Foo<T,> = T;
```

When the last parameter goes, the whole `<...>` list is removed.

No fix is offered for:
- type parameters of interfaces and classes, since those can merge with other declarations that must declare identical type parameters;
- `infer` type parameters in conditional types, which can't simply be dropped.

It's marked dangerous because call sites or references that pass explicit type arguments (`foo<string, number>()`) will no longer match the new arity.

## Tests

New `test_type_parameter_remove_fix` in `tests/oxc.rs`. `cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib` (1292 passed), `cargo clippy -p oxc_linter --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` pass locally; CI also ran on my fork.

AI disclosure: this PR was written with AI assistance (code and description); I reviewed and tested it.

prs.title: fix(transformer): lower wrapped assignments and preserve computed receivers
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Normalize TypeScript-wrapped assignment targets before the parent expression reaches the JavaScript transforms. Previously, `(value as number) ||= 1` and `(value as number) **= 2` could retain unsupported operators in ES2015 output because target erasure happened after lowering inspected the assignment. Reuse the existing erasure path to preserve reference IDs and the lowerers' read/write bookkeeping.

Capture computed member receivers before evaluating nonliteral keys. This preserves the original object when key evaluation reassigns the receiver, including through `eval` or an imported live binding. Add static regressions for those cases alongside the wrapper matrix and update the affected expected outputs. The upstream `compoundAssignmentWithTypeOnlyExpressions.ts` transformer mismatch now passes.

feat(react-compiler): support logical assignment operators
prs.author: anonrig
prs.body:
**Why:** `??=`, `||=`, and `&&=` were a lowering Todo, so React Compiler skipped any component or hook that used one. Upstream `babel-plugin-react-compiler` still reports the Todo. Two upstream PRs that add support (react/react#36394, react/react#36733) were closed as stale, not rejected.

**What:**

- `a ??= b` lowers as `a ?? (a = b)` (likewise `||=` and `&&=`) with the value blocks of `LogicalExpression` lowering. The right side and the store only evaluate when the assignment is taken.
- The object and computed key of a member target, including identifier operands, are snapshotted before the property load so a getter cannot retarget the conditional store.
- Logical assignment to a `const` binding is a Todo (not a Syntax error). Emitting the store would rewrite `const` to `let` and swallow the runtime TypeError when the store is taken.
- `ref.current ??=` is treated as the same lazy initialization as `if (ref.current == null)`. A later read of `ref.current` during render is still reported. `||=` is not given that allowance.
- Fixtures: the two from react/react#36733, plus context/value-block, reference capture, const bailout, and ref lazy-init cases.

**Upstream divergence:** intentional. Marked with an "Unlike the TS implementation" comment. Upstream still Todos the operator and skips the function; the stale upstream PRs were not rejected. Identifier operands are also snapshotted (those PRs left plain identifiers unbound, which re-reads the binding after a getter).

prs.title: feat(data_structures): add `unreachable_unchecked!` macro
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Add an `unreachable_unchecked!` macro to `oxc_data_structures` crate.

Similar to `assert_unchecked!`, it's an unchecked assertion (undefined behavior if it is in fact reachable) in release builds, and a normal assertion in debug builds (panics if reached).

Unlike Rust's native `std::hint::unreachable_unchecked`, in debug builds it panics, rather than aborts, so the panic can be caught e.g. in conformance tests.

prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Building or checking a playground.oxc.rs share link is manual today: the URL packs the source, tab, options, lint rules, and formatter panels into query parameters. This adds a repository skill that does both directions so a reproduction can be shared and inspected consistently.

The encoder re-parses its own output before printing, so a malformed link is rejected instead of shared. The decoder preserves the state and writes the source only when asked, into a directory that must not exist yet. Both scripts resolve paths relative to the skill, so they work from any checkout.

Verified with `npx oxfmt --check`, Oxlint, `typos`, and an encode/decode round-trip of a transformer example. The encoder rejects malformed option JSON and the decoder reproduces the source byte for byte.
